decision: FIX consumer preparation using a shared build/test-only ECMAScript lock-v3 projection and npm ci --offline; KEEP Python HTTP-service orchestration.
constraints: Linux and Windows Node package tests and a Python HTTP-service harness must install the same packed SDK offline from integrity-verified cached archives, without registry packuments.
Retain npm verification, lifecycle-script denial, source/archive binding, exact runtime versions, public declaration and no-eval runtime checks.
Small committed flat runtime graph and local archive; reject unsupported lock formats, links or missing integrity. No package resolver, network fallback or full clean clone.

alternatives.technology: ECMAScript plus Node crypto and npm ci
alternatives.assessment: Selected shared adapter: both consumers already execute Node/npm; JSON lock projection and standard archive SHA-512 stay in that toolchain. npm remains the package graph/integrity verifier.

Technically capable and convenient for the service harness, but would require Python in the standalone Node package check or duplicate a versioned lock projection. Keep Python service lifecycle only and call the same local adapter.

Credible typed JSON processing and native standalone binaries, but this small build-only graph has no measured throughput constraint. It adds cross-platform binary/toolchain delivery without removing npm or improving its lock contract.

limits: The consumer fixture is generated from the committed project lock plus exact local archive bytes. It is not a claim that a tarball alone or an empty cache is installable offline.

The tarball-only regression cache is prepared from existing integrity-checked npm archives using the npm-bundled cacache API. No remote seeding occurs in that test; the documented API lookup is a tested npm toolchain dependency.
Locked same-version reinstall is tested; platform-wide installation, upgrades, signed releases, browser/hardware acceptance and P19 qualification remain open.
The adapter accepts this flat npm-v3 runtime graph, not arbitrary workspaces, peer/optional/link/nested package layouts. Reassess it if the committed graph changes.
